description: Composite figure: a temperature-time thermo-mechanical processing schedule carrying eight micrograph insets. The central schematic plots Temperature (°C) on the y-axis (gridline labels 700 °C and 1100 °C) against Time (hr) on the x-axis. From the 'Cast Sample' start point the path runs: Homogenisation 1100 °C (plateau), Water Quenching (down arrow), reheat to 1100 °C with a saw-tooth segment labelled Hot Rolling, Air Cooling, then Intercritical Annealing 700 °C (1 hr), and a final Water Quenching. Dotted arrows connect each stage to its microstructure. Eight labelled insets: M1-AC (100 µm bar) and M2-AC (200 µm bar) for the as-cast/homogenised state; M1-HQ (100 µm bar) and M2-HQ (500 µm bar) after water quenching; M1-HR (5 µm bar) and M2-HR (50 µm bar) after hot rolling (SEM-looking, fine banded relief); M1-IA (3 µm bar) and M2-IA (5 µm bar) after intercritical annealing (SEM-looking, banded two-phase structure). The '1' and '2' series track the two alloy variants (with and without Si). The figure demonstrates the complete processing route used and the microstructure obtained after every step, linking each thermo-mechanical condition to its micrograph.

observations.observation: The central schematic plots Temperature (°C) versus Time (hr) with printed y-axis gridline labels at 700 °C and 1100 °C.

The processing route begins at a point labelled 'Cast Sample' and includes Homogenisation at 1100 °C, Water Quenching, Hot Rolling at 1100 °C, Air Cooling, Intercritical Annealing at 700 °C (1 hr) and a final Water Quenching.
Eight microstructure insets are labelled M1-AC, M2-AC, M1-HQ, M2-HQ, M1-HR, M2-HR, M1-IA and M2-IA, each with a printed scale bar.
The printed scale bars are 100 µm (M1-AC), 200 µm (M2-AC), 100 µm (M1-HQ), 500 µm (M2-HQ), 5 µm (M1-HR), 50 µm (M2-HR), 3 µm (M1-IA) and 5 µm (M2-IA).
Dotted arrows link each processing stage of the temperature-time path to the corresponding labelled micrograph.
Hot rolling is drawn as a saw-tooth (multiple-pass) segment at 1100 °C rather than a flat plateau.
The caption states the figure is a schematic illustration of thermo-mechanical processing together with the observed microstructures after each processing step.
The citing text states that Fig. 3 displays the schematic representation of all processing steps used in this work, with sample-condition nomenclature given in Table 1.

The citing text states samples were etched with 2 % Nital solution (2 ml nitric acid + 98 ml ethanol) for 10-15 s and imaged by optical microscope (OM) and scanning electron microscope (SEM), with EBSD for crystal orientation.
Two parallel sample series (suffixes 1 and 2) are tracked through identical processing stages, consistent with the two alloy variants of the study.

The micrographs at the later processing stages (M1-HR, M2-HR, M1-IA, M2-IA) are rendered at much smaller scale bars (3-50 µm) than the as-cast/quenched ones (100-500 µm), indicating finer features are resolved after rolling and annealing.

subfigures.description: Schematic temperature (°C) vs time (hr) thermo-mechanical processing route: Cast Sample → Homogenisation 1100 °C → Water Quenching → Hot Rolling at 1100 °C → Air Cooling → Intercritical Annealing 700 °C (1 hr) → Water Quenching. Y-axis ticks printed at 700 °C and 1100 °C.
Optical micrograph of as-cast/homogenised condition M1, 100 µm scale bar; fine etched granular/dendritic contrast.
Optical micrograph of as-cast/homogenised condition M2, 200 µm scale bar; coarse etched grain structure.
Micrograph of water-quenched condition M1, 100 µm scale bar; lath/needle-like martensitic contrast.
Micrograph of water-quenched condition M2, 500 µm scale bar; lighter matrix with scattered dark features.
Micrograph of hot-rolled condition M1, 5 µm scale bar; fine banded/lamellar relief, SEM-like.
Micrograph of hot-rolled condition M2, 50 µm scale bar; banded grey relief, SEM-like.
Micrograph of intercritically annealed condition M1, 3 µm scale bar; banded two-phase structure with dark and light constituents, SEM-like.
Micrograph of intercritically annealed condition M2, 5 µm scale bar; alternated light/dark bands, SEM-like.
